subject.title: feat(ui): approval UX overhaul — inline cards, fair queue, shortcuts, badges

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this multi-surface approval UX now, or should the work be narrowed to a smaller approved approval-flow improvement?
rationale: The branch introduces new interaction patterns across approval queueing, inline chat, keyboard actions, and navigation indicators; correctness fixes alone cannot establish that this is the desired permanent product model.

options.title: Sponsor and repair the full UX
options.body: Keep the broad direction, resolve the two UI defects, and require live after-fix proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Retain a smaller approved subset such as fair queue ordering and one presentation surface, leaving shortcuts and badges for a follow-up.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Pause this PR until an owner defines the permanent approval interaction model and accessibility requirements.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and repair the full UX
recommendation.body: Keep the broad direction, resolve the two UI defects, and require live after-fix proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context shows the most direct recent work and assignment on this approval UX, though broader ownership needs a repository-history check.
